versions: Only the ask has two versions (agency, brand). A visitor from neither home gets the brand wording, as on the flicker page. Key phrases are written between double stars, as in flicker.json.

title: Checking a test
before launch.
head.titleNote: The second part is set in italic.
head.intro: A test can be wrong in ways nobody sees at first glance. I look for them before your customers find them.

plate.label: A proof sheet: the tested page, and a street scene of the test, with six marks

instruction.desktop: Watch the street · open the six marks
instruction.phone: Watch the street · tap the six marks

sides.store: The store · what your visitors see

sample.note: The made-up sample page of the agencies home. On the phone drawing the button text is cut on purpose: it is fault 1.

sentence.start: This test looks ready to launch.
sentence.end: Six faults, corrected before launch. On a real test I find them, **before your customers do.**
sentence.endNote: The key phrase is set upright in paper-copper, not bold.

ticket.note: In a fault, the key phrase is set in red, not bold. In a check, it is set in bold.

marks.fault: The button text is **cut** on a phone.
marks.howICheck: I open both versions **on a phone and on a desktop** before launch.

marks.fault: The button is pressed, the cart **stays empty.**
marks.howICheck: I go **to the end** in both versions: add to cart, then checkout.
I follow **one visit** and read what the test records for it.

marks.markLabel: Mark 4: The old button shows first
marks.howICheck: I watch the page **load slowly**: nothing may change in view.

marks.markLabel: Mark 5: Also on a sold-out product
marks.fault: A **sold-out product** gets the test too.
marks.howICheck: I open **the pages around it**: the test must show only where it was ordered.
I **switch it off** before launch and check that every page goes back.

title: Six checks.
Then the doors open.
lamps.titleNote: The second part is set in italic, in the accent colour.
lamps.label: The store of the plate with six lit lamps, numbered one to six, above its name. Its doors A and B are open; the gentleman stands in front.

title: After launch,
your customers find it.
afterLaunch.text: A fault that passes the launch is met by **real customers, on the real store**. And what the test counted until then **cannot be trusted**: the test has to start again, and the days it ran are lost.
afterLaunch.label: The gentleman looks at the counter of the test, back to zero. The leaves of a calendar lie in a heap at the foot of a poster column, a broom against it.

title: What it means
for you.
forYou.text: I go through **every test before it goes live**, whether I built it or **someone else did**. You get **a short written note**: what I checked, what I corrected. Then I **look again after launch**, to see that it still runs and counts as it should.
forYou.label: The gentleman reads a note on an easel: the six checks, each ticked, signed D. Castor.

scene.linesNote: The same six names as plate.marks[].check, in the order of the marks.

drawers.label: Other checks
drawers.question: What else do you check?
drawers.answer: The six on the plate are the ones every test needs. After them I check **what this test touches on your store**: other browsers and screen sizes, a customer who is logged in, a discount code, and **what the test sends to your analytics**.

drawers.label: Built by others
drawers.question: And a test built by someone else?
drawers.answer: I check it **the same way**. I do not need to have written it: I need **to open it on the store** before it goes live.

drawers.label: A fault found
drawers.question: And when you find a fault?
drawers.answer: If I built the test, **I correct it**. If someone else built it, I tell them **exactly what is wrong** and how to see it, and I can correct it if they ask.

ask.goesTo: The same place as on the flicker page: the closing ask of the home the visitor came from. A visitor from neither home: the letter slot of the brands home.
